matching.explanation: Unidentified finfish record classed by Sea Around Us as Medium demersals (30 - 89 cm); apportioned across the model's five multi-species guilds whose listed members are medium demersal or benthopelagic fish. Planktivores is excluded on size (every species Supplementary Table S1 lists there is under 30 cm) and Planktivores/Benthivores on habitat (its listed members are pelagic). Weighted by the catch composition of the identified taxa on those five groups.

Sea Around Us reports Northwest Pacific Sardinops (the Japanese pilchard) under this name; it is a small obligate filter-feeding planktivore. Supplementary Table S1 places the analogous clupeid Sardinella aurita in Planktivores.
Supplementary Table S1 defines Hairtails as the single species Trichiurus lepturus; this record is that species.

Obligate zooplanktivorous anchovy under 30 cm. Supplementary Table S1 places four engraulids (Thryssa dussumieri, T. vitrirostris, T. kammalensis, Stolephorus commersonnii) in Planktivores; the family is not confined to that group (Setipinna tenuifilis sits in Planktivores/Benthivores), so this is a guild judgement rather than containment.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Scomber japonicus under Planktivores/Benthivores; this record is that species.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Scomber japonicus in Planktivores/Benthivores; this genus-level record is that genus, and S. japonicus is the East China Sea Scomber stock.

Pacific saury is an epipelagic zooplanktivore feeding on copepods and euphausiids, matching the model's plankton-feeding guild; Supplementary Table S1 gives Planktivores a correspondingly mixed roster of small pelagic and mesopelagic filter feeders.

Phylum-level record, but Sea Around Us classes it Other demersal invertebrates with a trophic level of 2.10, which matches the benthic filter feeders of the Mollusks group ('Bivalves' Supplementary Table S1, model TL 2.17) and not the model's separate Cephalopods group (TL 2.82-2.96), whose catch this dataset reports under its own labels.

Aggregate crustacean landing classed by Sea Around Us as Shrimps; the model's only two harvested crustacean compartments are Shrimps (13 penaeid, sergestid and caridean species Supplementary Table S1) and Crabs (six portunids). Benthic Crustaceans is excluded because Supplementary Table S1 defines it as Gammaridea and Cumacea, which the fishery does not land. Apportioned by the catch composition of the identified crustaceans in this LME.

Aggregate crustacean landing classed by Sea Around Us as Shrimps; the model's only two harvested crustacean compartments are Shrimps (13 penaeid, sergestid and caridean species Supplementary Table S1) and Crabs (six portunids). Benthic Crustaceans is excluded because Supplementary Table S1 defines it as Gammaridea and Cumacea, which the fishery does not land. Apportioned by the catch composition of the identified crustaceans in this LME.
Supplementary Table S1 defines Small yellow croakers as the single species Larimichthys polyactis.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Acetes chinensis under Shrimps; this record is another species of that listed genus.

Japanese flying squid, an ommastrephid fall inside the model's Cephalopods group, whose members Supplementary Table S1 gives as ten squid, cuttlefish and octopus species (Uroteuthis edulis, Sepia esculenta, Octopus ocellatus, Ommastrephes bartrami and others).

Family-level record. Supplementary Table S1 distributes the model's sciaenids across six groups: Johnius belangerii and J. distinctus in Benthivores, Pennahia argentata in Piscivores, Atrobucca nibe and Miichthys miiuy in Benthivores/piscivores, Nibea albiflora and Collichthys lucidus in Omnivores, Larimichthys crocea and L. polyactis in their own single-species groups. Apportioned by the catch composition of the identified taxa on those groups.

Threadsail filefish is a small demersal picker on benthic invertebrates; Supplementary Table S1 places the analogous small demersal invertebrate feeders, including the tetraodontiform Diodon holocanthus and the apogonid Ostorhinchus angustatus, in Benthivores.
Supplementary Table S1 defines the model's Mollusks group as 'Bivalves'; this record is a bivalve.
Supplementary Table S1 defines the model's Other invertebrates group as 'Cnidaria'. True jellyfishes are scyphozoan cnidarians and this is the model's only compartment for them.

Righteye flounders are demersal feeders on polychaetes, small crustaceans and bivalves, matching the Benthivores definition of Supplementary Table S1 (Parapercis sexfasciata, Acanthocepola limbata, Uranoscopus japonicus, Johnius spp.).
Supplementary Table S1 lists Muraenesox cinereus under Piscivores.

Supplementary Table S1 lists this species twice, as 'Pennahia argentata' under Piscivores and as 'Pennahia argentatus' under Benthivores/piscivores. The paper's discussion resolves the duplication by naming 'benthivores/piscivores (Pennahia argentatus and Nemipterus virgatus)', and the species' diet of shrimps, crabs and small fish matches that guild. This corrects an inherited assignment to Piscivores.

Pacific cod is a large demersal generalist taking crabs, shrimps, polychaetes and fish, functionally the model's mixed benthivore-piscivore guild (Nemipterus virgatus, Miichthys miiuy, Atrobucca nibe). No gadid appears in Supplementary Table S1 and the species reaches only the northern margin of the East China Sea, so this is analogy, not the paper.

Family-level filefish record. Supplementary Table S1 places the one monacanthid in the model, Aluterus monoceros, in Planktivores/piscivores; the filefish that dominates East China Sea landings, Stephanolepis cirrhifer, is a small benthic invertebrate feeder matching the Benthivores definition, whose listed members include the analogous tetraodontiform Diodon holocanthus. Apportioned by catch composition.

Family-level filefish record. Supplementary Table S1 places the one monacanthid in the model, Aluterus monoceros, in Planktivores/piscivores; the filefish that dominates East China Sea landings, Stephanolepis cirrhifer, is a small benthic invertebrate feeder matching the Benthivores definition, whose listed members include the analogous tetraodontiform Diodon holocanthus. Apportioned by catch composition.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Pampus chinensis and Pampus argenteus in Planktivores/piscivores; this genus-level record is that genus.
Supplementary Table S1 defines the model's Mollusks group as 'Bivalves'; this record is a bivalve.
Supplementary Table S1 lists 'Trachypenaeus curvirostris' under Shrimps, the historical combination of this species.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Nemipterus virgatus in Benthivores/piscivores; this genus-level record is that genus.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Scomberomorus niphonius and S. guttatus in Piscivores; this genus-level record is that genus.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Portunus trituberculatus under Crabs.

Octopuses fall inside the model's Cephalopods group, whose members Supplementary Table S1 gives as ten squid, cuttlefish and octopus species (Uroteuthis edulis, Sepia esculenta, Octopus ocellatus, Ommastrephes bartrami and others).

Cuttlefishes and bobtail squids fall inside the model's Cephalopods group, whose members Supplementary Table S1 gives as ten squid, cuttlefish and octopus species (Uroteuthis edulis, Sepia esculenta, Octopus ocellatus, Ommastrephes bartrami and others).
Supplementary Table S1 defines Large yellow croakers as the single species Larimichthys crocea.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Scomberomorus niphonius under Piscivores; the paper's discussion names it as the group's exemplar.

So-iny mullet feeds on benthic diatoms, detritus and meiofauna. The model has no herbivore or detritivore fish compartment, so Benthivores, its only bottom-feeding guild, is the closest available home; the mismatch in diet is real and a reviewer may prefer to leave mullets unresolved.

Squids fall inside the model's Cephalopods group, whose members Supplementary Table S1 gives as ten squid, cuttlefish and octopus species (Uroteuthis edulis, Sepia esculenta, Octopus ocellatus, Ommastrephes bartrami and others).

Fleshy prawn fall inside the model's Shrimps group, which Supplementary Table S1 fills with thirteen penaeid, solenocerid, sergestid and caridean species including Metapenaeus joyneri, Parapenaeopsis hardwickii and Metapenaeopsis barbata.

At sea Pacific salmon feed on euphausiids, amphipods, squid and small fish, which is the mixed plankton-and-fish guild the model defines with Decapterus maruadsi and Trachurus japonicus. The model has no anadromous or subarctic compartment and no salmonid appears in Supplementary Table S1, and salmon reach the East China Sea only at its northern margin, so this is an analogue placement a reviewer may prefer to leave unresolved.

Family-level record. Supplementary Table S1 places the model's carangids in exactly two groups: Decapterus maruadsi, Trachurus japonicus and Parastromateus niger in Planktivores/piscivores, and Caranx sexfasciatus in Omnivores. Apportioned by the catch composition of the identified carangids in this LME.

Family-level record. Supplementary Table S1 places the model's carangids in exactly two groups: Decapterus maruadsi, Trachurus japonicus and Parastromateus niger in Planktivores/piscivores, and Caranx sexfasciatus in Omnivores. Apportioned by the catch composition of the identified carangids in this LME.

Supplementary Table S1 lists this exact species twice, once under Planktivores/Benthivores and once under Planktivores/piscivores, and gives no basis for preferring either; the candidate set is therefore exact but the split is arbitrary, so equal weights are used.

Supplementary Table S1 lists this exact species twice, once under Planktivores/Benthivores and once under Planktivores/piscivores, and gives no basis for preferring either; the candidate set is therefore exact but the split is arbitrary, so equal weights are used.

Mantis shrimps are stomatopods, not decapods, and appear nowhere in Supplementary Table S1, but Sea Around Us classes them under Shrimps and the East China Sea trawl fishery lands them with the shrimp catch; the model has no other compartment of comparable size and habitat (Benthic Crustaceans is defined as Gammaridea and Cumacea).
Porgies and seabreams take a wide mix of benthic invertebrates, algae and small fish; Supplementary Table S1 places the sparid Acanthopagrus schlegelii in Omnivores.
Crevalles are small carangids taking zooplankton and small fish; Supplementary Table S1 places the comparable carangids Decapterus maruadsi and Trachurus japonicus in Planktivores/piscivores.

Cuttlefishes fall inside the model's Cephalopods group, whose members Supplementary Table S1 gives as ten squid, cuttlefish and octopus species (Uroteuthis edulis, Sepia esculenta, Octopus ocellatus, Ommastrephes bartrami and others).

Supplementary Table S1 defines Bombay duck as Harpadon nehereus; the same species is also listed under Piscivores, but the dedicated single-species group is the model's own compartment for this stock and takes the record.

Skipjack tuna is an epipelagic piscivore; Supplementary Table S1 puts the comparable scombrid Auxis thazard and the epipelagic Coryphaena hippurus in Piscivores, so the model's top fish-eating guild does extend to oceanic predators.

The cephalopod class record fall inside the model's Cephalopods group, whose members Supplementary Table S1 gives as ten squid, cuttlefish and octopus species (Uroteuthis edulis, Sepia esculenta, Octopus ocellatus, Ommastrephes bartrami and others).
Supplementary Table S1 lists the nemipterid Nemipterus virgatus in Benthivores/piscivores; this family record is that family.
Yellowfin tuna is an epipelagic piscivore; Supplementary Table S1 places the scombrid Auxis thazard and the epipelagic Coryphaena hippurus in Piscivores.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Trachurus japonicus under Planktivores/piscivores.
Supplementary Table S1 defines the model's Other invertebrates group as 'Cnidaria'. The flame jellyfish are scyphozoan cnidarians and this is the model's only compartment for them.

Flathead grey mullet feeds on benthic microalgae and detritus; the model has no herbivore or detritivore fish group, so it is placed in the only bottom-feeding guild, with the same caveat as the other mullets.

Penaeoid prawns fall inside the model's Shrimps group, which Supplementary Table S1 fills with thirteen penaeid, solenocerid, sergestid and caridean species including Metapenaeus joyneri, Parapenaeopsis hardwickii and Metapenaeopsis barbata.
Red seabream is a generalist on crustaceans, molluscs, echinoderms and small fish; Supplementary Table S1 places the sparid Acanthopagrus schlegelii in Omnivores.

Order-level record spanning both of the model's decapod compartments. Sea Around Us classes it Lobsters, crabs and the same dataset carries separate Dendrobranchiata and Brachyura records, so this residual is reptant-dominated; catch-composition weighting, which favours Shrimps, is therefore a lower bound on the crab share.

Order-level record spanning both of the model's decapod compartments. Sea Around Us classes it Lobsters, crabs and the same dataset carries separate Dendrobranchiata and Brachyura records, so this residual is reptant-dominated; catch-composition weighting, which favours Shrimps, is therefore a lower bound on the crab share.

The horned turban fall inside the model's Mollusks group by name, but Supplementary Table S1 states its composition as bivalves only, so a gastropod is included on the group's taxonomic name rather than on its listed membership.
Whitespotted conger takes both benthic crustaceans and small fish; Supplementary Table S1 places the congrid Ariosoma anago in Benthivores/piscivores.

Family-level record. Supplementary Table S1 splits the model's congrids: Uroconger lepturus and Rhynchoconger ectenurus sit in Benthivores while Ariosoma anago sits in Benthivores/piscivores. Apportioned by catch composition.

Family-level record. Supplementary Table S1 splits the model's congrids: Uroconger lepturus and Rhynchoconger ectenurus sit in Benthivores while Ariosoma anago sits in Benthivores/piscivores. Apportioned by catch composition.
Amberjacks are large carangid piscivores, unlike the plankton-and-fish scads Supplementary Table S1 lists in Planktivores/piscivores; they belong in the model's fish-eating guild.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Ilisha elongata (spelled 'Ilisha elongate') under Omnivores.
Rockfishes are demersal ambush predators taking both benthic crustaceans and fish, the mixed guild of Supplementary Table S1 (Nemipterus virgatus, Priacanthus macracanthus).
Groupers are ambush piscivores on the shelf and its hard bottoms, matching the model's fish-eating guild.

Pencil squids fall inside the model's Cephalopods group, whose members Supplementary Table S1 gives as ten squid, cuttlefish and octopus species (Uroteuthis edulis, Sepia esculenta, Octopus ocellatus, Ommastrephes bartrami and others).
Supplementary Table S1 lists the stromateids Pampus chinensis and Pampus argenteus in Planktivores/piscivores; this family record is that family.

True crabs fall inside the model's Crabs group, which Supplementary Table S1 fills with six portunids (Portunus trituberculatus, Charybdis feriatus, C. bimaculata, P. sanguinolentus, C. acuta, P. argentatus).

Octopuses fall inside the model's Cephalopods group, whose members Supplementary Table S1 gives as ten squid, cuttlefish and octopus species (Uroteuthis edulis, Sepia esculenta, Octopus ocellatus, Ommastrephes bartrami and others).

Family record for filter-feeding herrings and sardines; Supplementary Table S1 places the clupeid Sardinella aurita in Planktivores. The one clupeiform the paper puts elsewhere, Ilisha elongata (Omnivores), is reported separately by Sea Around Us.
Pacific sandlance is a small copepod-feeding schooling fish under 30 cm, matching the Planktivores roster of Supplementary Table S1.
Supplementary Table S1 defines the model's Mollusks group as 'Bivalves'; this record is a bivalve.
Rainbow sardines are small round herrings feeding on zooplankton, the functional type Supplementary Table S1 lists in Planktivores as Sardinella aurita.

Family-level record. Supplementary Table S1 places Scomber japonicus in Planktivores/Benthivores and Scomberomorus niphonius, S. guttatus and Auxis thazard in Piscivores, so the family spans exactly these two groups. Apportioned by catch composition.

Family-level record. Supplementary Table S1 places Scomber japonicus in Planktivores/Benthivores and Scomberomorus niphonius, S. guttatus and Auxis thazard in Piscivores, so the family spans exactly these two groups. Apportioned by catch composition.
Largetooth flounders are ambush piscivores as adults, unlike the invertebrate-feeding righteye flounders, so they belong in the model's fish-eating guild.

The model has one shark group (Scoliodon laticaudus Supplementary Table S1) and no ray group: Supplementary Table S1 places the batoids Narcine lingula and Dasyatis zugei in Benthivores. A record spanning sharks, skates and rays is therefore apportioned between those two groups by catch composition.

The model has one shark group (Scoliodon laticaudus Supplementary Table S1) and no ray group: Supplementary Table S1 places the batoids Narcine lingula and Dasyatis zugei in Benthivores. A record spanning sharks, skates and rays is therefore apportioned between those two groups by catch composition.
Dotted gizzard shad is a small clupeid filter feeder on phytoplankton and zooplankton, matching Planktivores, where Supplementary Table S1 places Sardinella aurita.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Auxis thazard in Piscivores; this genus-level record is that genus.
Supplementary Table S1 lists the tetraodontid Lagocephalus spadiceus in Benthivores/piscivores; this family record is that family.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Pampus argenteus under Planktivores/piscivores.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Priacanthus macracanthus in Benthivores/piscivores; this genus-level record is that genus.

Supplementary Table S1 lists the synodontid Saurida tumbil in Piscivores; this family record is that family. The one synodontid the model treats separately, Harpadon nehereus, is reported under its own Sea Around Us name.
Bastard halibut is an ambush piscivore taking mainly fish and squid as an adult.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Coryphaena hippurus under Piscivores.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Nemipterus virgatus under Benthivores/piscivores; the paper's discussion names it as an exemplar of that group.

Family record for the same marginal salmonid catch as the Oncorhynchus record; placed by analogy in the mixed plankton-and-fish guild, with the same caveat that the model has no anadromous compartment.

Blue swimming crab fall inside the model's Crabs group, which Supplementary Table S1 fills with six portunids (Portunus trituberculatus, Charybdis feriatus, C. bimaculata, P. sanguinolentus, C. acuta, P. argentatus).
Supplementary Table S1 lists Sardinella aurita in Planktivores; this record is another species of that listed genus.

The genus Charybdis fall inside the model's Crabs group, which Supplementary Table S1 fills with six portunids (Portunus trituberculatus, Charybdis feriatus, C. bimaculata, P. sanguinolentus, C. acuta, P. argentatus).
Supplementary Table S1 defines the model's Mollusks group as 'Bivalves'; this record is a bivalve.
Supplementary Table S1 defines the model's Mollusks group as 'Bivalves'; this record is a bivalve.
Sea urchins fall inside the model's Echinoderms group, which Supplementary Table S1 represents by Ophiuroidea and which is the model's only echinoderm compartment.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Decapterus maruadsi under Planktivores/piscivores; the paper names it the group's dominant species in M1997.
Japanese seabass takes both shrimps and fish in coastal and estuarine water, matching the mixed benthivore-piscivore guild of Supplementary Table S1.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Priacanthus macracanthus under Benthivores/piscivores.

Flyingfishes are epipelagic zooplanktivores feeding on copepods and other small crustaceans, matching the Planktivores guild rather than the carnivorous Omnivores roster of Supplementary Table S1 (Nibea albiflora, Acanthopagrus schlegelii, Caranx sexfasciatus).
Supplementary Table S1 lists the congener Scomber japonicus in Planktivores/Benthivores; blue mackerel is the same genus with the same mixed plankton-and-benthos diet.
Supplementary Table S1 defines the model's Mollusks group as 'Bivalves'; this record is a bivalve.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Atrobucca nibe under Benthivores/piscivores.
Silver-stripe round herring is a small schooling zooplanktivore, the Planktivores type of Supplementary Table S1 (Sardinella aurita, Thryssa spp.).
Oilfish is a deep-slope gempylid taking fish, squid and crustaceans; Supplementary Table S1 places the gempylid Rexea prometheoides in Benthivores/piscivores.
Snappers are nocturnal predators taking mainly fish and large crustaceans, matching the model's fish-eating guild.
Rockfishes and thornyheads are demersal ambush predators on crustaceans and fish, matching the model's mixed benthivore-piscivore guild.

Okhotsk atka mackerel is a semi-pelagic zooplanktivore, feeding mainly on copepods and euphausiids in midwater and secondarily on benthos, so it belongs with the model's mixed plankton-and-benthos guild rather than with the piscivorous hexagrammid Hexagrammos. This corrects an inherited assignment to Benthivores/piscivores.

Deepsea smelts are small mesopelagic zooplanktivores. Supplementary Table S1 places the mesopelagic myctophid Benthosema pterotum, the group's dominant species, in Planktivores, so the model's plankton-feeding guild is where mesopelagic filter feeders belong.

Order-level record. Supplementary Table S1 places clupeiforms in three groups: Thryssa dussumieri, T. vitrirostris, T. kammalensis, Stolephorus commersonnii and Sardinella aurita in Planktivores, Setipinna tenuifilis in Planktivores/Benthivores, and Ilisha elongata in Omnivores. Apportioned by the catch composition of the identified clupeiforms.

Order-level record. Supplementary Table S1 places clupeiforms in three groups: Thryssa dussumieri, T. vitrirostris, T. kammalensis, Stolephorus commersonnii and Sardinella aurita in Planktivores, Setipinna tenuifilis in Planktivores/Benthivores, and Ilisha elongata in Omnivores. Apportioned by the catch composition of the identified clupeiforms.

Order-level record. Supplementary Table S1 places clupeiforms in three groups: Thryssa dussumieri, T. vitrirostris, T. kammalensis, Stolephorus commersonnii and Sardinella aurita in Planktivores, Setipinna tenuifilis in Planktivores/Benthivores, and Ilisha elongata in Omnivores. Apportioned by the catch composition of the identified clupeiforms.
Goatfishes sift the sediment with their barbels for polychaetes and small crustaceans, the Benthivores definition of Supplementary Table S1.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Chelidonichthys kumu under Benthivores.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Nibea albiflora in Omnivores; this record is another species of that listed genus.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Saurida tumbil under Piscivores.
Mullets are detritus and benthic microalgae feeders and the model has no herbivore or detritivore fish compartment; placed in the only bottom-feeding guild, with the diet mismatch noted.
Supplementary Table S1 lists Coryphaena hippurus in Piscivores; this genus-level record is that genus.
Albacore is an epipelagic piscivore, the functional type Supplementary Table S1 places in Piscivores as Auxis thazard and Coryphaena hippurus.
Bartail flathead is a sand-ambush predator taking mainly fish and large shrimps.
Supplementary Table S1 defines the model's Mollusks group as 'Bivalves'; this record is a bivalve.
Supplementary Table S1 lists the muraenesocid Muraenesox cinereus in Piscivores; this family record is that family.
Dogfish sharks fall inside the model's Sharks group, which Supplementary Table S1 represents by Scoliodon laticaudus and which is the model's only shark compartment.
Yellowtail amberjack is a large carangid piscivore taking mainly fish and squid, matching the model's fish-eating guild rather than the plankton-and-fish scad guild.

Swimming crabs fall inside the model's Crabs group, which Supplementary Table S1 fills with six portunids (Portunus trituberculatus, Charybdis feriatus, C. bimaculata, P. sanguinolentus, C. acuta, P. argentatus).
